items.item_text: Current California RN License
Basic Life Support (BLS) from American Heart Association or American Red Cross.
Baccalaureate degree in Nursing. If the Baccalaureate degree is not in Nursing, a Master’s degree in Nursing is required
3 years of recent ambulatory clinical care experience*, preferably in an urgent care or emergency department setting (staff nurse/charge nurse/manager).

Take on a key clinical leadership role within a world-class, award-winning health system. Take your career in an exciting new direction. You can do all this and more at UCLA Health. As RN Supervisor you will be responsible for assisting with clinical management and administrative coordination for the Beverly Hills Wilshire, Specialty Care clinic. The position is a combination of clinical (direct patient care) and administrative nursing responsibilities.

We’re seeking an experienced RN with supervisory experience to lead and support our clinical team. In this vital role, you’ll provide hands-on patient care while ensuring an efficient workflow of our back-office team at UCLA Health Beverly Hills Wilshire, Specialty Care clinic. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
Performing patient assessment, care, and education to pediatric and adult patients in a clinical/urgent care setting
Supervising and training clinic nursing staff
Working closely with physicians to manage patient care; triage phone and in-basket messages for providers
Collaborate with the Practice Manager and Clinical Director to ensure seamless clinical operations
Planning and adjusting staffing to meet operational needs efficiently
Responsible for the management of the Quality Assurance and audit process; responsible for ordering clinic supplies and medications
Pay Rate: $132,300.00 to $307,100.00 annually.
Behaviors, actions, and language reflect conscious commitment to supporting unit, department, and hospital vision
Pediatric Advanced Life Support (PALS) from American Heart Association or American Red Cross
Projects a calm, reassuring and confident manner and promotes a cohesive team environment
Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS) from American Heart Association or American Red Cross
Consistently achieves high standards in clinical duties and holds self to same standards as others are held to
Makes decisions in the best interest of the patient
Effectively listens and communicates to peers both positive and constructive feedback
Consistently uses good judgment in making decisions
Consistently identifies opportunities to improve unit performance and takes action to implement ideas
Develops rapport with patients and patients’ families
Able to recognize (or bring attention to) peers’ accomplishments
Maintains positive attitude towards unit and work, helping to build unit’s positive reputation
Consistently models right behaviors
developing a plan of care including setting goals, monitoring and documenting progress
implementing interventions that are pertinent to goals established in the plan of care
evaluating the effective of interventions toward the attainment of established goals and
recognizing the need to reassess or reset goal parameter
Able to admit fault and acknowledge others’ position without becoming defensive
